provenance.marketVsCatalyst: Asian equity rebound observed; oil and rate impact on US cash remains prospective.

editorial.marketOverview: Asian equities extended their rebound, with AP reporting Kospi up 4.2% and Japanese chip equipment shares recovering. AP also reports higher crude prices, while WSJ reports a 4.921% US ten-year yield. US cash remains closed ahead of the shortened Friday session.
editorial.whatChanged: Compared with 01:20 ET, the Asian rebound has broader reported support. AP oil quotations are higher than the prior Reuters report, but exact timestamps and contract synchronization are unavailable. Open Watch remains at 181 events. No material new catalyst established.
editorial.marketInterpretation: Overnight risk appetite is improving, but the repository early outlook at 01:21 ET shows a Nasdaq score of -49 and VXN 38.53 versus VIX 26.80. These are dashboard observations with unknown underlying timestamps, not live cash confirmation. Rates and crude remain valuation risks; no causal US cash reaction can yet be measured.
editorial.threeDayPath: Friday: relief rally potential with fade risk in thin liquidity. Monday: normal liquidity and Sunday OPEC+ outcome test sustainability. Tuesday: JOLTS and tentative semiconductor earnings may redirect rates and leadership.
editorial.bullCase: Broad cash QQQ and SOX leadership, falling volatility and retreating crude and yields would support a durable reversal. Asian chip recovery is encouraging but insufficient alone.
editorial.bearCase: Failure to hold overnight gains alongside weak chips and elevated yields or crude would reinforce downside risk. Holiday liquidity can amplify either direction.
editorial.watchNext: Confirm paired Treasury yields, cash SOX relative strength, Nasdaq breadth and VXN/VIX after reopening. Watch Friday 13:00 ET close, Sunday OPEC+ and Tuesday JOLTS; earnings dates remain tentative.
